exposure: Meconium microbiome composition (alpha diversity, relative abundance of Bifidobacterium pseudolongum)
higher relative abundance of Bifidobacterium pseudolongum in meconium
mode of delivery (cesarean vs. vaginal birth)
Infants born by Caesarean section; total subjects (both Caesarean and vaginal)
finding: Higher meconium microbiome alpha diversity and higher relative abundance of Bifidobacterium pseudolongum were associated with lower risk of neonatal jaundice, particularly in infants born by Caesarean section.
mod_finding: Higher meconium microbiome alpha diversity was associated with lower risk of jaundice in cesarean-born infants but not in infants born vaginally.
